EconomyMines.HelpTitle: How does the Mine Report work?
EconomyMines.HelpPurpose: Compute your province's weekly mine report: production, upkeep and miners' salary, ready to share on the forum.
EconomyMines.HelpOverview: Two ways to use this chest: a quick daily report to post on the forum (paste today's text, then click straight on "Format today's report", no calculation, no week to pick), or a priced weekly report (steps below).
EconomyMines.HelpStep1: Pick the week you want to process with the arrows at the top of the page — only days within that specific week will be taken into account, even if your pastes contain others.
EconomyMines.HelpStep2: In the game, open the "Management of the mines" tab and copy the whole page text, starting from "Maintenance costs increase..." through to the end of the page.
EconomyMines.HelpStep3: Paste that text into the Mines Commissioner's Log. You can paste the interface several times to complete the data for the selected week: each new paste fills in the data already known, without ever erasing anything.
EconomyMines.HelpStep4: Click "Generate weekly report": it computes the production value, upkeep and net (after salary) for the selected week.

RegistryPage.HelpPurpose: The registry keeps the record of the province's mines, from one office-holder to the next. The Mines Superintendent, the Sheriff, the Trade Minister and the province's leader read it; only the first two record reports in it, from the Mines report.
RegistryPage.HelpOverview: The page has two columns: on the left what helps you decide (the report, then your term), on the right the registry's memory (levels and recorded reports). Nothing is deleted: a replaced report stays visible in the history.
RegistryPage.HelpStep1: Last report, top right: it turns orange if it is two days old or more.
RegistryPage.HelpStep2: Current report: output, value, wages, upkeep and balance of each mine since the start of your term's month (1st month from when you took office, 2nd month from mid-term), up to yesterday. It stays provisional until the month ends. The arrows replace it with a week of your term, recomputed day by day with the prices in force that day; "Current period" brings back the month.
RegistryPage.HelpStep3: Reports for your term: at mid-term and at the end of the term, computed from the reports recorded since you took office. Before the date, the page only says in how many days.
RegistryPage.HelpStep4: Days without data: the days no report covers. A paste contains the game's last 7 days, so a day without a paste is not necessarily lost.
RegistryPage.HelpStep5: Before you took office: the reports recorded by other characters in the 30 days before. This section only appears when there are some.
RegistryPage.HelpStep6: Level history: a rise is an improvement; a drop with no upkeep recorded while the threshold had been reached is shown in red; any other drop is a deliberate choice. A mine whose level changed several times unfolds.

Registry.HelpPurpose: The registry keeps the record of the province's mines, handed from one office-holder to the next. The Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff record reports in it; the Trade Minister and the province's leader can read them.
Registry.HelpOverview: Each entry keeps the pasted text, the parsed report, and the prices and miners' wage/hour in force on its date in the province, signed by your character and its office. A report is never deleted: an incorrect report is replaced, and the old one stays visible in the history.
Registry.HelpStep1: Paste the contents of the "Management of the mines" tab, as for the report. Today's prices and wage/hour are shown as a reminder: they come from the province's price table and are managed from the registry page.
Registry.HelpStep2: Check the province shown: it is the province of your office, not of your residence.
Registry.HelpStep3: Click "Record in the registry". The report takes the date of the last day in its data: an older paste fills in a missing day without replacing today's.
Registry.HelpStep4: A report is already recorded today in the province? The Office tells you and names who recorded it. Yours only replaces it once you confirm, and only if it brings something new: an identical report, or one that says less, is refused.

decode.Name: Crack the Code
decode.Description: A hall of sealed chests awaits you. Invite your community to crack their codes: each participant tries a 5-digit combination, you enter their guess, and the mechanism reveals how many are well placed. The first to find them all opens the chest — and the overall ranking recounts everyone's feats.
decode.Rules:
The Office des Coffres provides you with a room full of sealed chests. Each chest is locked by a secret combination of five digits (0 to 9). To try to crack one open, submit your combination to the room's organiser.

For each attempt, the chest's mechanism responds:
— 2 points for each digit in the correct position,
— 1 point for each digit present in the combination but in the wrong position.

The maximum score for an attempt is 10 — five digits, all in the right place. If you reach it, the chest opens and we move to the next — you earn a bonus of 10 for cracking the chest!

The overall standings track the points accumulated by each participant. Good luck!

Cookies.Preamble: This page describes how the officedescoffres.creacube.be site uses cookies and local storage technologies in your browser. It complements the {privacyLink}, which covers personal data associated with your account.

Section1.Title: 1. Reminder: non-official tool
Section1.Content: Office des Coffres is a non-official community tool for the game Renaissance Kingdoms, developed voluntarily. It is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by Celsius Online, the game's publisher.

Section3.Title: 3. What we store in your browser
Section3.Intro: No third-party HTTP cookies are set on this site. We use two browser storage mechanisms, both limited to what is strictly necessary:

Preferences.Title: Local storage — Preferences
Preferences.Purpose: remember your interface choices (dark/light theme, French/English language), your default character, and your last inputs in public tools (Watch, Mines Report, Crack the Code).
Preferences.Data: your chosen theme, language, default character ID, cache of texts you have pasted into public tools, and the address of the last Crack the Code activity you created or opened in public mode on this device.
Preferences.Retention: until you clear site data from your browser, or withdraw your consent via the cookies banner.
Preferences.LegalBasis: your consent (GDPR art. 6.1.a, article 129 of the Belgian law of 13 June 2005 on electronic communications, transposing the ePrivacy Directive).
Preferences.IfDecline: the site works normally, but your preferences and drafts are not remembered between visits.

Tokens.Title: Local storage — Authentication tokens
Tokens.Purpose: maintain your connection to your user account during your session.
Tokens.Data: an access token (short-lived) and a refresh token (longer-lived if you check "Stay logged in").
Tokens.Retention: access token valid for 15 minutes; refresh token valid for 12 hours by default or 30 days if you checked "Stay logged in".
Tokens.LegalBasis: these tokens are strictly necessary for the service requested (your login). As such, they are exempt from consent under article 129 of the Belgian law of 13 June 2005 on electronic communications, but documented here for transparency.
Tokens.IfDecline: you cannot stay logged in — you would need to re-authenticate on each action, making usage impractical.

Section4.Title: 4. What we don't do
Items: No audience measurement or behavioral analytics cookies (Google Analytics, Matomo, Plausible, etc.).
No data sharing with third-party services for commercial purposes.
No sale of information to anyone.

Section5.Title: 5. Technical note: HTTP cookies vs local storage
Section5.Content: Technically, this site does not use "cookies" in the classic HTTP sense. It uses the browser's localStorage mechanism to store preferences and authentication tokens. This distinction is purely technical — from the perspective of the GDPR and the Belgian APD (Data Protection Authority), both mechanisms fall under the same information and consent obligations, and are treated identically in this policy. The term "cookies" is used in the consent banner for general understanding.

Section6.Title: 6. Distinction between anonymous visitor and registered user
Section6.Anonymous: Anonymous visitor (no account): only the Preferences storage can be enabled, based on your choice in the cookies banner. Nothing else is stored.
Section6.Registered: Registered user with an account: authentication tokens are added to local storage when you log in. Your account data itself (characters, account preferences) is stored on our server, not in your browser — see {privacyLink}.

Section7.Title: 7. Your rights
Section7.Withdraw: Withdraw consent at any time via the "Manage preferences" button in the navigation. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before withdrawal.
Section7.Erase: Erase stored data: clearing your site data from your browser (Settings → Privacy → Clear data) instantly removes everything stored on the browser side.
Section7.Complaint: Right to lodge a complaint with the {apdLink} if you consider that the processing of your data does not comply with GDPR.

Section8.Title: 8. Changes to this policy
Section8.Content: This policy may be modified to reflect technical or regulatory changes. Any substantial modification will be signaled by a re-opening of the consent banner on your next visit. The date of last modification is indicated at the bottom of this page.

Section9.Title: 9. Contact
Section9.Content: For any question related to this policy or the exercise of your rights, contact: {emailLink}

Data.Intro: For each tool of the Office: what it is for, what you put into it, what is stored, for how long, who sees it, and what happens if you delete your account. The rules that apply to the whole Office (legal bases, rights, security, hosting) are in the {privacyLink}.
Data.Upcoming: Upcoming: this tool is not open yet. What follows describes what it will store as soon as it opens.
Data.Access: Most of the Office's tools work without an account: everything happens in your browser, and the Office keeps nothing. An account becomes necessary as soon as you want the Office to keep what you produce. Finally, a few tools act on behalf of an office in your province: to use the Mine Registry you must hold the Mines Superintendent's or the Sheriff's office and have had it validated in the Office — this is not optional, it is the condition of access.
Data.SeePolicy: What is stored, for how long, who can access it and what happens if you delete your account: see the {privacyLink} (§3 to §6).

Account.Title: Account and characters
Account.Text: Your account (email address, password) and your characters (name, town of residence, validation status): what is stored, why, on which legal basis and for how long is described in the {privacyLink} (§3 to §5). This page does not repeat it.

Offices.Title: Declared offices and My province
Offices.Purpose: Have the office your character holds recognised (mayor, or county councillor and their title), so that the tools know who may write on behalf of a function, and keep your province's office history ("My province" page). An account is needed.
Offices.InputLead: Declaring an office is optional — except for the tools that require one.
Offices.Input: You can use the Office without declaring any function. However, a tool that acts on behalf of a province function, such as the Mine Registry, only opens to a declared and validated office.
Offices.InputDetail: You then provide the office (mayor, or county councillor and their title), the city or province, the dates of the term and the link to the public announcement.

MinesReport.Title: Mines report
MinesReport.Purpose: Format the report from the "Management of the mines" tab and compute your mines' weekly report, to share on the game forum. No account is needed.
MinesReport.Input: The text you copy from the "Management of the mines" tab: each mine's state, its hours worked, its output and the resources consumed. It contains no player name.
MinesReport.Stored: Nothing is stored on our servers: the calculation happens in your browser. If you have accepted preference cookies, your browser keeps, for each week, the merged pasted reports, along with the prices and hourly rate you entered, so you find them again at your next paste. Without that consent, nothing is kept.
MinesReport.Duration: In your browser, until you clear the site's data or withdraw your consent to preference cookies, which erases them immediately.
MinesReport.Audience: No one but you: this data does not leave your browser, except what you choose to publish on the game forum.
MinesReport.Deletion: No effect: the Mines report is not tied to any account.

MineRegistry.Title: Mine Registry
MineRegistry.Purpose: Keep a province's mine management record, handed from one office-holder to the next: the Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff save their reports to it, and the Trade Minister and the province's leader (count, duke…) may read them. You must hold one of these offices in the province, and have had it validated in the Office. Without that, the tool is not available. It also holds the province's mine prices, set by the Trade Minister, the Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff.
MineRegistry.Input: The same text as for the Mines report: the contents of the "Management of the mines" tab, copied from the game. For prices: the price of each resource and the hourly wage, with the date they take effect.

Watch.Title: Watch
Watch.Purpose: Compare two lists of your town's villagers copied from the game, to see who came in and who left, and prepare the forum message. No account is needed.
Watch.Input: Two lists of villagers copied from the game: they contain other players' character names.
Watch.Stored: Nothing is stored on our servers: the comparison happens in your browser. If you have accepted preference cookies, your browser keeps the last list you pasted, to offer it as "yesterday's list" on your next visit. Without that consent, nothing is kept.
Watch.Duration: In your browser, until you clear the site's data or withdraw your consent to preference cookies, which erases them immediately.
Watch.Audience: No one but you: this data does not leave your browser, except what you choose to publish on the game forum.
Watch.Deletion: No effect: the Watch is not tied to any account.

Map.Title: Kingdoms map
Map.Purpose: Pick a town from the game's reference list of kingdoms, provinces and towns, for instance when creating a character, changing residence or requesting an office. No account is needed.
Map.Stored: No personal data: the map is the same for everyone, and it knows nothing about you.

Privacy.Preamble: This page describes how the officedescoffres.creacube.be site processes the personal data associated with your user account. It complements the {cookiesLink}, which covers local storage in your browser.

Section1.Title: 1. Reminder: non-official tool
Section1.Content: Office des Coffres is a non-official community tool for the game Renaissance Kingdoms, developed voluntarily. It is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by Celsius Online, the game's publisher.

Section3.Title: 3. When you create an account
Section3.Intro: Creating a user account is optional. The site can be browsed freely without an account, with access to public tools (Watch, Mines Report). A free account unlocks additional features tied to your game history (Customs, Mines Registry — upcoming modules).
Section3.AccountFieldsIntro: To create an account, only two pieces of information are requested:

AccountFields.Label: Email address
AccountFields.Text: used for login, identity verification on first access, and service-related communication (password reset, important notifications).

AccountFields.Label: Password
AccountFields.Text: stored securely (hashed with bcrypt), never in plain text.

Section3.CharacterFieldsIntro: You can then add one or more Renaissance Kingdoms characters to your account:

CharacterFields.Label: Character pseudonym
CharacterFields.Text: as it appears in the game.

CharacterFields.Label: City of residence
CharacterFields.Text: selected from the official reference of kingdoms/provinces/cities.

CharacterFields.Label: Validation status
CharacterFields.Text: indicates whether the character has been verified as legitimate by an administrator.

CharacterFields.Label: Declared offices (optional)
CharacterFields.Text: the office (mayor, or county councillor and their title), the city or province, the dates of the term and the link to the public announcement, which you provide to have your authority validated in the modules, as well as the history of your council offices.

Section3.MineRegistryIntro: If you are the Mines Superintendent or the Sheriff of a province and you save a report to the Mine Registry, the Office stores:

MineRegistryFields.Label: The text you paste
MineRegistryFields.Text: the contents of the game's "Management of the mines" tab as you copy it. It is kept verbatim, so that a later correction to the parsing also applies to reports already saved.

MineRegistryFields.Label: The parsed report
MineRegistryFields.Text: per mine: level, output, hours worked, resources consumed, deterioration threshold, and the date of the report.

MineRegistryFields.Label: Prices and hourly rate
MineRegistryFields.Text: the prices and wage/hour in force in your province on the report's date, kept with it because they change over time. They come from the province's price table (see below), not from anything you type.

MineRegistryFields.Label: Province and office
MineRegistryFields.Text: the province where you hold your office — not your town of residence —, the office used (Mines Superintendent or Sheriff), and the character who saved the report.

Section3.MinePricesIntro: If you are the Trade Minister, Mines Superintendent or Sheriff of a province and you record or correct that province's mine prices, the Office keeps:

MinePricesFields.Label: The prices
MinePricesFields.Text: the price of each resource and the miners' hourly wage, with the date they take effect. A price stays in force until the next one.

MinePricesFields.Label: The province
MinePricesFields.Text: your office's province, not your city of residence.

MinePricesFields.Label: Who recorded it
MinePricesFields.Text: the character who recorded the price and the one who last corrected it, with the date and time.

Section3.AnimDecodeIntro: Crack the Code, an Animation module activity, can be played two ways. In private mode, the activity is linked to your character, which carries everything needed: nothing more is asked, and the activity disappears with your character or your account (see §5). In public mode, to create and manage an activity without using a character, the Office stores:

AnimDecodeFields.Label: A nickname
AnimDecodeFields.Text: the one you choose to be identified as the organiser on the activity's public page — required, so you can be contacted if needed.

AnimDecodeFields.Label: A password
AnimDecodeFields.Text: chosen by you, stored hashed (never in plain text), to prove you are the organiser for every management action. You can reset it via your confirmed email address, or by requesting a reset from the site administrator.

AnimDecodeFields.Label: An email address (optional)
AnimDecodeFields.Text: if you provide and confirm it via the link we send you, it lets you reset your own password, be warned each time it is changed, and receive a full report of your activity when it closes. Without a confirmed address, a reset remains possible by contacting the site administrator. An address provided but not confirmed is never used.

AnimDecodeFields.Label: A fingerprint computed from your IP address
AnimDecodeFields.Text: a one-way fingerprint (HMAC-SHA256): it lets us recognise the same connection to check that you are not creating several public activities at once, but we cannot recover the underlying address from it. It is erased as soon as your activity closes.

Section3.AnimDecodeNote: In both modes, the nicknames you enter for the proposals you receive — whoever attempted a combination, whoever cracked the chest — are freely typed by you, from what you receive (forum, newsletter, in-game). We do not verify them, and they are not linked to any account.
Section3.ToolsIntro: What each tool is for, who can use it, what you put into it and what it does or does not store is explained tool by tool on the {dataLink} page:

Section4.Title: 4. What we do with your data

Rows.Purpose: Authenticate you, contact you for service needs
Verify your identity on each login
Operate private tools tied to your account (upcoming: Customs, Mines Registry)
Verify that you have access to the declared address
Access control to administration functions reserved for the site editor
Check your office, then tell the modules who may write on behalf of a position

Section4.NoCommercialUse: No personal data is used for commercial, advertising, aggregate statistics, or profiling purposes.

Section5.Title: 5. How long we keep your data
Section5.ActiveAccount: Active account: your data is kept as long as your account exists.
Section5.InactiveAccount: Inactive account: after 1 year without login, your account may be automatically deleted, following a notice email to the declared address.
Section5.UnverifiedAccount: Unverified account: if the email address is not confirmed, the account is deleted after 30 days, and no sooner than one week after a reminder sent to that address.
Section5.DeletedAccount: Deleted account: immediate and definitive deletion of the associated personal data (email, hashed password, linked characters).
Section5.TechnicalLogs: Technical logs (server access, application errors): kept for a maximum of 12 months for incident investigation and service security, then erased.
Section5.Mandates: Declared offices: your requests and terms, including ended, rejected or revoked ones with their reason, are kept as long as your account exists. When your character or your account is deleted, everything is erased EXCEPT the history of offices held: your character's name, the office, the province or city, the dates and how the office ended. This information is public in the game; what remains is a pseudonym and a role, and the Office no longer keeps anything linking that pseudonym to you (no email address, no account).
Section5.MineRegistry: Mine Registry: the reports you save are kept with no time limit, because together they form a province's management record, handed from one office-holder to the next. If you delete your character or your account, the report remains, but its link to your account is removed: it keeps its date, its province and the office used, and no longer names any character. We say "the link is removed" rather than "the report is anonymised": the province's office history remains available, and it may allow a date and an office to be matched to a character name. Finally, no report can be deleted, not even by the person who wrote it: an incorrect report is replaced, and the replacement stays visible.
Section5.MinePrices: Mine prices: recorded prices are kept with no time limit, because they are used to compute the province's reports, from one office-holder to the next. You can correct a price while you hold the office, and up to 7 days after your term ends; after that it is locked. Successive price sets form a history and all remain viewable; however, correcting a set replaces its values, and the previous value is not kept. Nobody can delete a price. When your character or account is deleted, the prices stay, but their link to your account is removed: they keep their date and province and no longer name any character. Again, "the link is removed", not "anonymised": the province's office history may let someone match a date to a character's name.
Section5.AnimDecode: Crack the Code (Animation module): in private mode, the activity, its chests and the proposals you entered are kept for as long as you do not delete the activity, the character, or the account that created it — deleting any of those deletes the activity with them, chests and proposals included. In both modes, an activity with no action for 30 days is automatically closed; in private mode you can reopen it and everything is kept, whereas in public mode this closure is final: no reopening is possible. In public mode, on closing, whether manual or automatic, a report including all proposals received is sent to your email address if you confirmed one; the fingerprint of your connection, your email address, your password and any pending reset request are then erased. What stays visible to the community for 5 years after closing: the activity's name, your organiser nickname, the location, the chests cracked with the nickname of who found them, and the final standings — never the proposals received, which are erased on closing. After that period, the page and the nickname are deleted. To request the removal of a nickname entered on one of these pages before that period, contact {email}.

Section6.Title: 6. Who can access your data
Section6.Editor: The site administrator (see §2), for technical administration, user support and checking your office requests — access limited to the strict minimum.
Section6.NoOneElse: No one else beyond the above. No sharing, no resale, no transmission to third parties, including Celsius Online (publisher of Renaissance Kingdoms), except for a duly notified judicial requisition.
Section6.Hosting: Data is hosted on servers located in the European Union (host: o2switch, France).
Section6.ProvincePlayers: Other players whose character resides in the same province, for that province's office history (character names, offices, dates, how each office ended) — including after your account is deleted, and which they may copy to the game forum. Never your email address, your pending requests, your rejections or the administration's notes.
Section6.MineRegistryHolders: The Mines Superintendent and the Sheriff of the province concerned, who keep that province's Mine Registry, as well as its Trade Minister and its leader (count, duke…), who may read it — including the office-holders who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. That is the registry's very purpose: a province's mines pass from hand to hand, and every office is vacated at each election. Never the other councillors, never a player from another province.
Section6.MinePricesHolders: Mine prices: the province's Trade Minister, Mines Superintendent and Sheriff, who manage them, and its leader (count, duke…), who may read them — including the office-holders who succeed you, and including after your account is deleted. The other holders of these three offices also receive, once a day, an email summarising the prices that changed and naming the character who changed them. Never the other councillors, never a player from another province.
Section6.AnimDecodeHolders: Crack the Code: an activity's public page (name, location, organiser nickname, chests cracked and standings) is visible to everyone, whether created in private or public mode — that is the point of this tool, shared on the game's forum. Your password is never visible to anyone, not even the site administrator. Your email address, if you confirmed one, is visible to the site administrator in the administration panel — to help you if you forget your password and for the technical administration of the service. Your organiser nickname and, if applicable, the date of the last password reset are also visible there.

Section7.Title: 7. Your GDPR rights
Section7.Intro: In accordance with articles 15 to 22 of the GDPR, you have the following rights over your personal data at any time:

Rights.Label: Right of access
Rights.Text: obtain confirmation that your data is being processed and receive a copy.

Rights.Label: Right to rectification
Rights.Text: correct inaccurate data about you (email and pseudonym editable from your Profile; other fields on request).

Rights.Label: Right to erasure ("right to be forgotten")
Rights.Text: request the deletion of your account and all associated data.

Rights.Label: Right to restriction of processing
Rights.Text: request the suspension of processing of your data in certain situations.

Rights.Label: Right to object
Rights.Text: object to the processing of your data based on legitimate interest.

Rights.Label: Right to data portability
Rights.Text: receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format (JSON), to transmit it to another service.

Section7.Complaint: Right to lodge a complaint with the {apdLink} if you consider that the processing of your data does not comply with GDPR.
Section7.HowToExercise: To exercise these rights: contact {email}. A response will be provided within a maximum of one month. Your account can be deleted immediately from your Profile; the email channel remains available as a fallback.

Section8.Title: 8. Security of your data
Section8.Intro: We implement the following technical and organizational measures to protect your data:
Measures: Passwords hashed via bcrypt (never stored in plain text, impossible to reconstruct).
OAuth 2.0 token authentication (Laravel Passport): short-lived access token (15 minutes) and separate refresh token (12 hours or 30 days with "Stay logged in").
Refresh token rotation on each use, with reuse detection (possible compromise signal).
Mandatory email verification before first login.
Administrator access restricted to a single role, manually assigned by the editor.
Section8.BreachNotice: No system being infallible, in the event of a security breach affecting your personal data, you will be notified in accordance with article 34 of the GDPR.

Section9.Title: 9. Cookies and local storage
Section9.Content: Browser-side storage (technical cookies, localStorage) is covered by a dedicated policy: {cookiesLink}. It notably describes the authentication tokens stored in your browser to maintain your login session.

Section10.Title: 10. Changes to this policy
Section10.Content: This policy may be modified to reflect technical or regulatory changes. Any substantial modification will be notified to you by email at the declared address. The date of last modification is indicated at the bottom of this page.

Section11.Content: For any question related to this policy or the exercise of your rights: {email}
